name: Synthetic ghost: Thomas pattern right, then burst both sides (Persinger 2000)
origin: Persinger, Tiller & Koren (Laurentian University), 2000 case study of one man who had experienced a haunt
summary: Persinger's lab tried to re-create one man's earlier 'haunt': 20 min of the frequency-modulated (Thomas) pattern mainly over the right hemisphere, then 20 min of the burst-firing pattern through both hemispheres. The lab reported rushes of fear and an apparition during the right-sided pattern and pleasant experiences during the bilateral one, in one subject without a sham session.
notes: One man wore a helmet with four solenoids per side, one left-right pair on at a time for 0.5 s. First came 20 min of the Thomas pattern (849 values, 3-ms points, 3 ms between repeats), set to favour the right: 5 uT at the right scalp and 1 uT at the left (Persinger 2000 p.3 [661]). The blindfold then came off for a questionnaire (p.4 [662]). Then came 20 min of the burst-firing pattern, 230 points of 3 ms (690 ms) 'once every 3,000 msec', equal on both sides, peak 2 uT at the scalp (p.5-6 [663-664]). This program plays the Thomas table (the first 849 values of Table 1 of US 6,234,953) as published, with the left side at a fifth, then the burst with a 3-s pause at 0.4 of the phase 1 level. The phases run back to back. The burst is rebuilt as this project's rising sweep with the published point duration and length; the point values were never published as numbers, only as a small graph (Persinger 2000 Fig. 2, p.5 [663]). One left-right pair is on at a time (0.5 s each), and the right side is reversed so that the pair's field points through the head. The four sites per side stand for the lab helmet's four solenoids per side on a 7.5 by 5 cm ellipse; the site names are this project's reading. This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. At 1 uT this helmet's field model gives about 24 uT at the scalp, about 5 times the paper's values. One subject, told he might or might not get a field, with no sham session: a case report. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). The lab reported fear in phase 1: press Skip to go to phase 2, and stop at once on fear or distress. Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history, implanted devices, pregnancy, or anxiety or trauma symptoms; have someone nearby.
setting: Seated in a quiet room that is dark except for one small red light, with the eyes covered (the lab used modified swimmer's goggles in an acoustic chamber). The subject was told he might or might not receive a field, and EEG was recorded at F7, F8, T3, T4, O1 and O2.
schedule: One session in the original. At most weekly; for a self-test, use the app's Blind option and write down what you felt before unblinding.
